Nb (110). Single-crystal Nb films are first prepared on A-plane sapphire,
followed by the evaporation of Al in an O2 background. The first stages of
Al2O3 growth are layer-by-layer with hexagonal symmetry. Electron and x-ray
diffraction measurements indicate the Al2O3 initially grows clamped to the Nb
lattice with a tensile strain near 10%. This strain relaxes with further
deposition, and beyond about 5 nm we observe the onset of island growth.
Despite the asymmetric misfit between the Al2O3 film and the Nb under-layer,
the observed strain is surprisingly isotropic.

We study the possibility of obtaining large nongaussian signatures in the
Cosmic Microwave Background in a general class of single-field nonlocal
hill-top inflation models. We estimate the nonlinearity parameter f_{NL} which
characterizes nongaussianity in such models and show that large nongaussianity
is possible. For the recently proposed p-adic inflation model we find that
f_{NL} ~ 120 when the string coupling is order unity. We show that large
nongaussianity is also possible in a toy model with an action similar to those
which arise in string field theory.

Text: We investigate theoretically the capabilities of coherent correlation spectroscopy (CCS) for probing exciton dynamics in semiconductors.   Two common theoretical frameworks, the sum-over-states (SOS) approach and the quasiparticle picture, are compared for their ability to describe CCS signals.   The SOS approach provides a complete description of excitonic coherence but can be computationally demanding for large systems.   In contrast, the quasiparticle picture offers a more tractable approach but neglects certain aspects of exciton correlations.   We demonstrate that femtosecond time-resolved CCS experiments can provide insights into both individual exciton states and their collective behavior.

At intermediate intercalation levels, a sharp transition occurs in the persistence length and entropic contributions to elasticity. Our results reveal that this transition correlates with cooperative binding effects and changes in the helical geometry. These findings provide insights into how intercalating agents modulate DNA mechanics and have implications for understanding drug-DNA interactions and DNA packaging in biological systems.

particular emphasis on the production of high-energy photons and neutrinos. The

detail. Prospects for future observations at different wavelengths of this type

Text: The multiferroic compound DyMnO3 exhibits a polarization flop transition at low temperatures, accompanied by changes in magnetic structure. Using high-resolution neutron diffraction and polarization measurements, we demonstrate the absence of commensurate magnetic ordering at this critical transition. The magnetic structure remains incommensurate throughout the polarization flop process, contrary to predictions from conventional magnetoelectric coupling theories. Our findings reveal that the transition mechanism involves continuous evolution of the incommensurate modulation vector rather than a lock-in to commensurate phases. This discovery provides new insights into the microscopic origin of multiferroicity in rare-earth manganites and challenges existing theoretical frameworks for understanding polarization control through magnetic field manipulation in these systems.

We extend this formalism to interacting electron systems, incorporating many-body effects through perturbation theory and Green's function techniques. The generalized theory enables calculation of magnetization in correlated materials where interactions significantly modify electronic structure. Applications include ferromagnetic and paramagnetic systems, with particular emphasis on transition metals and strongly correlated compounds, providing insights into magnetocrystalline anisotropy and orbital contributions to magnetic moments.

Microfabrication of graphene devices used in many experimental studies
currently relies on the fact that graphene crystallites can be visualized using
optical microscopy if prepared on top of silicon wafers with a certain
thickness of silicon dioxide. We study graphene's visibility and show that it
depends strongly on both thickness of silicon dioxide and light wavelength. We
have found that by using monochromatic illumination, graphene can be isolated
for any silicon dioxide thickness, albeit 300 nm (the current standard) and,
especially, approx. 100 nm are most suitable for its visual detection. By using
a Fresnel-law-based model, we quantitatively describe the experimental data

detect and recover this information, using the probability distribution

and phase structure quantity. We show that ALMA, with its high dynamical range,
is definitely needed to achieve significant detection of phase structure, and
that it will do so even in the presence of a fair amount of atmospheric phase
noise. We also show that ALMA should be able to recover the actual "amount" of
phase structure in the noise-free case, if multiple configurations are used.

Our findings indicate that the joint entropy exhibits oscillations around its steady-state value, with a frequency related to the inter-particle interaction energy.

is turned on or off by changes in the concentration of a transcription factor
(TF). We use recent data on noise levels in gene expression to show that it
should be possible to transmit much more than just one regulatory bit.
Realizing this optimal information capacity would require that the dynamic
range of TF concentrations used by the cell, the input/output relation of the
regulatory module, and the noise levels of binding and transcription satisfy
certain matching relations. This parameter-free prediction is in good agreement
with recent experiments on the Bicoid/Hunchback system in the early Drosophila

The exchange parameters yield an effective magnetic coupling constant of approximately 8 meV, consistent with experimental observations. These findings establish Ba2CoS3 as a model low-dimensional magnetic material exhibiting quasi-one-dimensional behavior with significant inter-chain coupling effects influencing the long-range ordering mechanism.

dissipated in the outer solar layers. Progress in this field has been slow and

obtained, in arbitrary dimensions, by explicitly computing the cohomology of
the corresponding Becchi-Rouet-Stora-Tyutin differential in the space of
integrated local functions at ghost number unity. This provides a purely
algebraic, regularization-independent classification of the Weyl anomalies in
arbitrary dimensions. The so-called type-A anomaly is shown to satisfy a
non-trivial descent of equations, similarly to the non-Abelian chiral anomaly
in Yang-Mills theory.
